title: Post Missam ad tabernam
summary: Sunday: Mass with the family, then the pub, where Marcus drinks only water. Is the pub after Mass a good custom? Quotes: Īte, missa est (end of the Latin Mass), In vīnō vēritās (old proverb; Pliny the Elder), Tū servāstī bonum vīnum ūsque adhūc (John 2:10).

intro.en: Today, let's talk about Sunday: Mass, the pub… and water.
intro.la: Hodiē loquāmur dē diē Dominicō: dē Missā, dē tabernā… et dē aquā.

lines.en: So, Marcus. What did you do on Sunday?
lines.la: Ergō, Marce. Quid diē Dominicō fēcistī?

lines.en: In the morning we went to Mass. All of us.
All of you? Who?
With my wife, my two daughters, and my son.
lines.la: Cum uxōre meā, duābus fīliābus, et fīliō.

lines.en: I have two daughters and one son. Five people in one row.
lines.la: Duās fīliās et ūnum fīlium habeō. Quīnque hominēs in ūnō ōrdine.

lines.en: And the little one? Was he quiet?
Quiet? No. [light chuckle] He talked the whole time.
lines.la: Tacuit? Minimē. [light chuckle] Tōtum tempus loquēbātur.

lines.en: And at the end, he shouted: Amen!
He was listening, though.
Do you know how the old Latin Mass ended?
lines.la: Scīsne quōmodo Missa Latīna antīqua fīniēbātur?

lines.en: No. Tell me.
The priest said: Ite, missa est.
That is: go, now it's over. And that's where the name Missa comes from.
lines.la: Id est: īte, nunc fīnis est. Et inde venit nōmen Missa.

lines.en: [thoughtful] So the Mass is named after its last words.
lines.la: [thoughtful] Ergō Missa nōmen ā verbīs ultimīs habet.

lines.en: And after Ite, missa est… we went.
lines.la: Et post Īte, missa est… īvimus.

lines.en: Where did you go?
After Mass, we came to the pub.
[dry] Almost right.
Almost? What did I get wrong?
Nothing. [light chuckle] I wanted to talk like your teacher.
lines.la: Nihil. [light chuckle] Sīcut magistra tua loquī volēbam.

lines.en: Please, correct only one mistake. And only real ones.
lines.la: Ūnum tantum errōrem corrige, quaesō. Et tantum vērōs.

lines.en: Fine, fine. Let's go on.
So. The pub. What did you eat?
The others ate meat. A lot of meat.
I ate only vegetables.
Only vegetables? Why?
Because tomorrow I have a meeting with my clients.
lines.la: Quia crās conventum cum clientibus meīs habeō.

lines.en: And I want a clear head.
And what did you drink? Wine? Beer?
I drank only water. Only water.
[a little more serious] Water. At the pub. On a Sunday.
lines.la: [a little more serious] Aquam. In tabernā. Diē Dominicō.

lines.en: Marcus, the Romans used to say: in wine, there is truth.
lines.la: Marce, Rōmānī dīcēbant: in vīnō vēritās.

lines.en: Who said that?
It's an old proverb. Pliny the Elder writes about it.
lines.la: Vetus prōverbium est. Plīnius Maior dē eō scrībit.

lines.en: Wine opens the mouth; then people tell the truth.
lines.la: Vīnum ōs aperit; tum hominēs vērum dīcunt.

lines.en: So in water there is… nothing?
In water there's only water. [light chuckle]
lines.la: In aquā tantum aqua est. [light chuckle]

lines.en: Fine. Tomorrow, after the meeting, I'll drink wine.
lines.la: Bene. Crās, post conventum, vīnum bibam.

lines.en: May I ask a serious question?
Of course.
First Mass, then the pub. Is that a good custom, in your opinion?
lines.la: Prīmum Missa, deinde taberna. Estne bona cōnsuētūdō, tuā sententiā?

lines.en: Hmm… yes, I think so.
At Mass, we are with God.
At the pub, we are with our friends.
Both are good. Both are human.
But some people say: the pub after Mass? That's not holy.
lines.la: Sed quīdam dīcunt: taberna post Missam? Nōn sānctum est.

lines.en: [matter-of-fact] Even Jesus went to a wedding. And he made wine.
lines.la: [matter-of-fact] Etiam Iēsus ad nūptiās iit. Et vīnum fēcit.

lines.en: At Cana. In the Gospel of John, chapter two.
lines.la: In Cānā. In Ēvangeliō Iōannis, capite secundō.

lines.en: And a man there said: you have kept the good wine until now.
lines.la: Et aliquis dīxit: tū servāstī bonum vīnum ūsque adhūc.

lines.en: Until now! Ūsque adhūc. I like that.
Because the best wine came last.
Like my wine… [lightly amused] tomorrow, after the meeting.
lines.la: Sīcut vīnum meum… [lightly amused] crās, post conventum.

lines.en: So the debate is over?
It's over. Mass, the pub, wine: all good.
lines.la: Fīnīta est. Missa, taberna, vīnum: omnia bona.

lines.en: And water?
Water… is for the magpies.
[light chuckle] Goodbye, Marcus. Good luck tomorrow!
lines.la: [light chuckle] Valē, Marce. Crās bona fortūna tibi sit!

lines.en: Thanks. Goodbye, Iulia!
